case.value: The bulls' case: Redfin and Mr. Cooper integration is compounding cross-sell (Redfin-sourced mortgage attach rate up to 47%, home-equity volume doubling y/y) and cost synergies ($100M realized in Q2 toward a $500M-by-2027 target), positioning Rocket to gain share and operating leverage once mortgage rates ease.

depends_on.value: Hitting the $500M annualized Mr. Cooper synergy run-rate by 2027 and continuing to grow the Redfin-to-Rocket mortgage attach rate; also needs mortgage rates to ease from currently elevated levels to unlock refi/purchase volume

why_it_fell.value: Down 42% from its 52-week high on a Q2 2026 miss (EPS and revenue both light) and a Q3 revenue guide ($2.5-2.7B) cut well below the $2.9B consensus, plus ongoing integration/execution risk on the Mr. Cooper and Redfin deals against a backdrop of still-elevated mortgage rates.

judgment.prospect_why: The case is Redfin and Mr. Cooper cross-sell delivering $500M of synergies by 2027, and it depends on both execution and rate relief; the last print missed on revenue and the Q3 guide was cut to $2.5-2.7B against $2.9B consensus, so the driver is not yet visible in the numbers.
judgment.competition_why: It is consolidating the industry rather than losing share, but it trades at 15.9x forward against UWMC at 4.2x and PFSI at 6.7x, a roughly threefold premium carried into a revenue miss and a guide cut, and mortgage origination has no gross-margin moat to read.
judgment.macro_fit_why: The worst macro fit in the set: a mortgage originator with TTM free cash flow of -$774M needs falling rates, and the market has flipped from pricing cuts to pricing roughly 1.5 hikes by December with the 10-year at 4.77%, so the thesis needs the regime to change.
judgment.narrative_why: Its only theme is rate relief, which the macro brief has moving the other way; there is no live narrative supporting it and no corpus account mentions it.
